title: 질문이용
text:
좋은 앱 만들어주셔서 고맙습니다
질문과 건의사항입니다
질문) 
무료체험 끝나구 1년짜리 구매하면 상대방한테 1년 선물할수 있는건가요?

건의사항입니다) 
제가 틈틈히 목표 사이에 ‘쉬기’ 를 많이 넣어야 하는데 이때마다 새롭게 생성해야 해서 번거로움이 있습니다. 

1. 하나를 생성하고 복붙할수 있는 기능이 있다면 반복작업이 필요할 때 도움이 될것 같아요 

2. 순서변경 시 굳이 오른쪽 위를 눌러 순서변경을 누르고  편집을 하는 것 보다 그 과정을 빼고 바로 꾹 누르는순서를 편집하는게 더 편리한것 같아요

3. 시간 설정시 —시간 —분 할때 예를 들어 30분을 할려다가 그냥 1시간 해야 겠다 싶으면 분 단위 스크롤을 다시 0분으로 돌리는게 번거롭습니다. 59분에서 0분으로 움직이는게 있으면 좋을 것 같습니다.

text:
안녕하세요, “루티너리” 라는 앱을 어제 다운받았지만, 굉장히 오래 쓸 거 같고, 좋은 앱이네요 :) 심플한 디자인과 타이머 기능, 직접 루틴 입력까지, 하나 아쉬운 것 없이 너무 좋아요. 일단 이런 앱을 개발하신 개발자님께 먼저 감사 인사를 전합니다 🙇‍♀️🙇‍♂️

다만, 한 가지, 아쉽다기보단 너무 속상하네요. 무료 기능은 루틴 설정이 최대 2개라는 게 너무 속상해요ㅜㅜ 물론 이렇게 좋은 앱을 유료 결제하는 것이 아까운 것보다는 현재 학생이고 작심삼일의 대명사(..?) 로 알려져 있어서...(유료 결제 후 안 쓴 적이 꽤...;) 부모님께서 결제는 안된다 하시더라구요...ㅠㅜ

하단에 광고를 넣거나, 타이머 종료 후 짧은 광고를 넣어도 좋으니 무료 버전도 최소 5개까지는 루틴을 만들어주셨으면 좋겠어요ㅠ 제 미래를 위해 한 번만 고려해주십쇼ㅠㅠㅠ

너무 무리한 요구였다면 죄송하고, 다시 한 번 감사의 말씀 전하겠습니다.

author: TeRiHo

text: 기능과 사용이 쉽고 좋으나 사용성은 고려되지 않은 것 같아요. 기본적으로 다른 어플에서 제공하는 반응과 너무 달라 동작 시 애를 먹습니다. 버튼마다 눌렀을 때 할 수 있는 행동이 너무 제한되어 있어요. '뒤로' 키가 먹지 않고 꼭 화살표나 '완료'를 눌러야 한다거나, 전체 행 선택이 안 되고 반드시 개발시 지정한 표시만 눌러야 작동이 된다거나.. 뭐 하나 수정할 때마다 암기력테스트.. 목적과 목표가 분명한 어플이라 사용 자체는 즐거우나 ux 진짜.. 거의 고려되지 않았다고 느껴요. 모든 액션이 너무 디테일하게 쪼개져있는데, 유저 입장에서 어떻게 쓰고 싶어할지 고민하시면서 개선하시면 좋을 것 같아요. 하나하나 말로 설명하기 어려울 정도로 동작이 제한적이라서 결제로 이어지기에는 제약이 되네요. 저 같은 유저는 이것 때문에 계속 대체재를 찾을거고, 찾는다면 이탈할 수 있을듯. 아 그리고 알람소리 너무 작고 짧아 폰의 노예처럼 들고다녀야 해요. 볼륨조절 가능하게 해주세요.
author: 2구구
developer_reply:

title: 습관 형성의 최고의 앱!
text:
먼저 이 앱을 개발해주셔서 감사합니다! 제가 정말 앱 리뷰를 남겨본 적이 없는데 한 번 써보고 너무 유용하고 더욱 더 발전되었으면 좋겠으면 하는 바램에 글을 남깁니다ㅎㅎ

아침에 일어나서 물 마시기, 흉터 연고 바르기 등 사소한 것들이라 아침에 놓치기 쉬운 행동들이 있어요. 
평소 제가 작심삼일이라 습관으로 형성되지 않는 것들이 수두룩한데, 정해놓은 루틴을 실행하기만 하면 생각할 필요 없이 따라하기만 하면 돼서 정말 직관적이고 좋아요ㅠㅠ!
여기에 습관으로 만들고 싶은 루틴들을 하나씩 추가해가면 더욱 유용하게 쓰고 싶어요! 

이 앱을 처음 써보고 나서 딱 느낀 점이 애플 워치랑 같이쓰면 정말 좋겠다는 것이었어요. 애플워치는 아직 구매 전이고 평소 필요성을 못 느껴왔었는데 이 앱 하나만으로 구매를 생각해보게 되었어요:) 루틴마다 폰을 항상 들고 다닐 수 없고 또 화장하기 전에 세균 가득한 폰을 만지는 것을 꺼리기 때문에 애플워치랑 루틴을 함께 한다면 정말 편할 것 같아요. 

다시 한 번 이 앱을 개발해주셔서 감사하고 더욱더 편리한 기능들을 기대할게요!

text: 결제해서 사용 중입니다. 좋은 앱이에요! 제게 습관에는 시간이 든 다는 것을 알려준 앱입니다. 그 전엔 그걸 몰라서 실패해왔던 것 같아요. 사용해보니 개선점도 몇가지 보이는데요, 1 시간을 정해두고 하는 일이 아닌, 체크 표시로 완료할 수 있는 항목도 있었으면 합니다. 예를 들면.. 제가 plastic zero를 실천하고자 하는데, 이건 하루를 회고하고 완료했는지 점검하는 일이라, 굳이 다른 앱을 사용해서 체크를 진행해야 하는게 아쉽습니다. 2 제가 요일별로 조금 다르게 변형해서 루틴을 사용중인데, 피드백은 각자 쌓이니 같은 습관이어도 피드백이 누적이 안되네요! 3 가능하다면 간단한 위젯을 만들어 주셨으면 합니다! 바탕화면에 깔아두면 동기부여가 더 잘 될 것 같아요. 4 Feedback 칸에 사진을 넣어도 좋을 것 같아요. 그리고 nike running app 처럼 완료 후 공유하는 기능이 있어도 좋겠단 생각을 했습니다. 좋은 앱 감사드려요!(갤럭시워치 연동 존버중입니다 아즈아)

title: iOS app great! Watch app won’t even open
text:
UPDATE: Watch app works now, although it seems things still get out of sync, and sometimes iOS app won’t open.

UPDATE #2: After updating some routines, watch app got out of sync again! Reinstalled watch app and now getting dreaded “Please open Routinery app on your iPhone”. This app is too unreliable for me considering I rely on the watch to run my routines.

——

ORIGINAL REVIEW:

First of all, I would like to say that the iOS app is fantastic and works very well to help you build habits and routines. That being said, the watch app has gone from finicky to working half the time to not even opening at all anymore which is *truly* disappointing.

I used to use the watch app independently of the phone, and it had some major syncing issues (usually one device lagging behind and then overriding the other’s progress), but it at least worked for the most part without having to open the phone app. This was helpful for those who want to eg avoid the distractions on their phone.

Then the watch app was changed to rely on the iOS app being opened first. I guess this was to fix the syncing issues, but it totally killed the ability to leave the phone behind and use only the watch, and wouldn’t work half the time without 1) starting a routine on the phone and 2) skipping/finishing some habits on the iOS app. Imagine the frustration when you have several routines.

Now the watch app crashes on startup regardless of the state of the iOS app. Basically, you can’t open it. It’s completely broken!

Even if the watch app is fixed so that it stops crashing, the fact that you must open the iOS app first (and start a routine on it) makes a watch-centered experience a distant dream, which is a real pity since it was mostly working before. I thought I had found my endgame routine app, but no longer. 🙁

iOS = great 
watchOS = currently 🗑🔥

title: My life is worse without Routinery
text:
Routinery revolutionized my morning and evening routines. This app is a timer. You list a sequence of tasks you need to do and how long each of the subtasks take. You start the timer, and the app displays one task on the screen. Press the check mark to move on to the next subtask. This app takes all the guess work out of everything. You focus on nothing but the task. And the timer reassures you that doing that dreaded chore does not actually take forever. 

I actually had stopped using this app for a few weeks. Editing the task was very confusing and cumbersome. But I will give this app another chance because I have to. I don’t think I can afford to not use this app. My quality of life has been noticeably worse without it.

If anyone is overwhelmed by using this app, I would start off by listing out every little thing. Once you develop good habits, you don’t need to keep everything anymore, maybe only the things you tend to avoid. 

As for feedback for the app, I still think the editing process needs some work. There’s a mode where you can change the order or delete, but you can’t edit the content of the task. That doesn’t make sense to my brain. Tapping the task should let me edit the contents, and a little “handle” at the end of the box can change the task order.

I don’t really use the contexts and feedback. It doesn’t make sense to me what they’re for because I can’t see the text when I’m in the middle of the routine. It could be useful if I could write a short sentence so I could read it while in the middle of the routine. But I can’t. 

Also, the motivational words at the top are a little weird sounding, like a non-native speaker of English. But this complaint doesn’t have to do with the function of the app, which is the most important thing.

Also lots of reviews talk about the app crashing. I have literally NEVER EVER had this problem.

As I start using this app again, I’ll update this review with more of my thoughts. I am just so passionate and grateful for this app. Everyone knows that not every product compels people to rave review it.

title: One of the best routine apps out there
text: The free trial version is great, and honestly better than a lot of the more expensive habit tracking apps out there. I’m surprised this app isn’t more popular! A few features that I really would love to see: - An simpler, untimed option where you can just see the current task to be done and check off when you’ve completed it. Some people can find being on a timer distracting and stressful - An option to automatically change certain tasks in a routine depending on days of the week. For example, under an exercise task an option to automatically have “Running” on Mondays and “Weights” on Tuesdays etc. - A timer and icon visual for the watch app - A one time purchase option with subscriptions These features would make the app so much better, but it’s still the best routine app I’ve used!

title: Seems nice, but the pricing is an obstacle for me
text:
I’ve used an app like this in the past, but I’ve been looking for a replacement because the old app doesn’t get updated anymore. This app seems like a good fit for me, but I’m put off by the fact that it’s only available as a subscription. Maybe I’m just old-school, but I really, really do not like subscription-based software. Trying to keep track of the various companies that want to automatically take my money at regular intervals is stressful and irritating. I don’t want money to leave my wallet until I press a button and make it happen myself.

I would be happy to pay more with a one-time purchase option, and the FAQ says that one may be added in the future, so I’m hopeful that will happen soon. If that happens, I would also be happy to support continued development with a “tip jar” type of option in the app, on top of the one-time payment.

title: Very disappointing - a great idea that doesn’t meet its potential
text: On the surface, it would seem Routinery is exactly the app I’m looking for. I’ve been trying to develop a morning routine for a while but always get distracted at some point, and rarely accomplished all my tasks. I was looking for an app that could keep me on task by attaching alarms and times to my to-do list. Routinery appeared to be the perfect fit and maybe it even has this functionality, but no matter how many times I tried I couldn’t get it to work. It doesn’t help that there is very little information provided on how to use it and no YouTube videos available showing how to set up basic functions. It also doesn’t help that the English on the site is replete with awkward phrasing and incorrect usage (the developers are Korean, but it’s unclear why they can’t hire a native speaker of English to edit their FAQ). The customer service provided is email only, and as nice as the Routinery people are, their recommendations never helped. You’d think making an app would be a lot harder than creating a YouTube video explaining how to use the app. It would also seem like finding a native speaker of English to edit your FAQ would be even easier (give any English speaker $20 and they could probably finish the job in 20 minutes). But for whatever reason the people at Routinery choose to not address these issues and the end result is an app that fails to rise to it’s potential:(

title: Going from chaos to order
text:
If you are someone who (like me):

1. Sees the necessity of routine
2. Kicks and screams and avoids stuff when it gets boring, and
3. Has tried every other time management program out there without success…

… this app could be the one for you!

It’s great for visual people. Specific, colourful icons make it fun and the clean design focuses your attention on what’s important.

It’s flexible. Skip, swap, delete and modify to your heart’s desire.

It will keep you on track. There’s a certain something about the timer that works so well where other things haven’t. It gets into your head and you can’t ignore it, even when you’ve skipped half of your routine and feel like chucking it in. You want to do better, and it helps you to, slowly but surely. 

I haven’t used all of the features yet, like the behavioural contexts or feedback, but it’s been worth every cent of the subscription price so far. Thank you, Developer! 

PS I have one suggestion… if it’s possible, a replica of the timer in the notification screen would be awesome 😊

title: I love the idea but…
text:
I honestly think the routine idea in this app is terrific! Also the inspirations from people is very motivating- I haven’t found an app that gets close to this one. I also like the design!
However, notifications do not work (I have an iphone XS max, dont know if that’s related) which is very annoying because I don’t check my phone every minute and often forget to validate each step. In the end, I end up with very long steps that I finished a long time ago and I can’t edit the durations. So my stats are not reliable at all and it’s difficult to keep track of an entire day routine for example…
Some features also have a weird UX, it’s not intuitive how to skip VS postpone and the wrong translations don’t help

Conclusion: huge potential and it would deserve a 5-star if there were no such constraints as the ones mentioned above…In the meantime, I don’t find it efficient to keep using it everyday but I hope the app gets better so I can get back to it

title: Wonderful for us with ADHD!
text:
This app has been such a blessing to me! A lot of us that suffer from ADHD have time blindness. We have no true concept of how much time a task actually takes us. This app gives me the independence to make my own schedule but gives me the accountability I need to actually see how much time it really takes me to do things and how I can adjust. For example, I’ve been using it the most on work days. Before Routinery, I was chronically late 10-15 mins for work. In my head, my morning routine takes 30 minutes. After Routinery, I learned it actually takes me an hour and 5 minutes to get ready for the day and leave on time. 

My mornings used to be so scattered (even on medication) and now it’s smooth sailing. I can even make time to sit on my couch, catch up on the local news, and drink my coffee. 

Thank you for this wonderful app!

title: 독보적 루틴 앱
text: 시중에 나와있는 거의 모든 할일앱과 습관앱을 다 써본 것 같은데요. 루티너리와 비교할 수 있는 다른 앱 자체가 없습니다. 앱이 얼마나 사용자 친화적이고 편한가도 다른 앱들과 비교불가하지만 무엇보다 루틴이 필요한 사람들이 어떤 라이프스타일을 원하는지 정확히 이해하고 있는 것 같은 점이 인상적이었어요. 명상이나 시각화, 목표에 대해서 생각 같은 루틴이 기본으로 들어가있다는 점에서 단지 하루하루를 생산적이게 사는 것에 치중한 것이 아니라 마음챙김이나 휴식의 요소들을 충분히 고려하고 있다는 인상도 받았구요. 루틴이라는게 단지 할일을 하나하나 해치우는게 아니라 전체적인 맥락이 있어야 한다는 점도 세심하게 반영한 것 같아서 너무 잘 쓰고 있습니다. 구독료가 하나도 아깝지 않네요.

title: Thank you for listening to feedback!!
text:
I’ve tried out a lot of apps like this and am a picky user. Routinery is the best one, hands down. The interface and features easily best the alternatives. 

The app now has the ability to mark off a task as done even after your routine is completed, which was the one thing keeping this amazing app from being perfect for me. I wrote in about this a few months ago and they said it was on the way, and it really is here! The other improvements, like being able to rearrange tasks DURING your routine have also been a great addition. 

I am not a naturally organized or routine person and years of health issues has made it worse -  this app makes such a difference for me. A must have if you’re easily distracted or struggle to remember routines. Thank you so much for this app!

title: Love (life changing), have some suggestions!
text:
I have ADHD and autism, so I always struggle with routine and organization, but also crave it and need it to function.

This app has made it possible for me to get out of bed on time in the morning, even if I’m tired. Why? Because the daily struggle and stress of trying to remember everything and the shame when I inevitably can’t or am late… is just GONE. I don’t have to use my brain right away, or stress out about forgetting anything, or decide what to do next. I’m not rushing. Even the boring stuff is easy. It’s easy to change the order of habits to optimize.

Also, the time tracking report (green/red with time differences) of individual habits for each completed routine is done very well, and is a GODSEND for my time blindness (I have no innate sense of time, and my house is covered with timers because of this.)

I’m rating this 5 stars because it is much better than anything else I’ve tried, and I love using it. It’s changing my life for the better. 

I do have a few suggestions:

1. Please add an option for unlimited reminders to start the next task! For those of us with ADHD, 5 is actually not enough. It’s easy to get absorbed in something and tune out the alarm, and then when all 5 go by I forget I was doing a routine. 

2. Please add an option for anytime-routines! Some routines are not planned at a specific time.

3. Please add an option to pause routines and have multiple on hold, or implement sub-routines that can be added to other routines! For example, one habit in my nighttime routine is to pack lunch for the next day, but sometimes I do that in the morning. I’d like to pause my main routine, go through the packing steps routine, and then finish that and continue with my main one. Not sure about the best way to make that work.

4. The icons are beautiful, but also not easy to navigate - the categories are a little arbitrary. It would be awesome if you could search for them using keywords or tags. I spend a LOT of time searching for an appropriate icon for each habit, which is time better spent creating the routine, and makes it harder for me to want to create new routines. Even easier would be an option to use an emoji as an icon, but the icons are beautiful, and I do love them. 

5. It would be nice to have an easy way to submit a request for a missing icon! For example, I would love a few different bags (duffel for gym, backpack, purse), as I spend a lot of time each day packing that stuff. An icon for “unpacking” would be amazing too. Or just the option to use emojis.

6. The time tracking summary after each routine is BEAUTIFUL, and it helps me so much. I wish there was a way to easily use the recorded time differences to update habit durations without having to switch screens so I could better learn how long individual things really take me. Writing them all down and then updating each habit in each routine individually is too much for me. 

7. Kinda related to 6: The same habits in different routines can have different duration settings (it’s like they are separate copies.) I wish there was a way to update the icons or durations of all copies at once from the original, or maybe have a way to apply it to all and de-select some, or have an option to enable or disable each habit added to a routine to sync updates from the original. 

8. An interactive tutorial would be great! I think I’m probably still missing things. 

Don’t take these suggestions as a reason not to use the app - it rocks!!! I’m a software developer so I just do this naturally, I can find problems with anything! I’m so grateful to the developers ❤️

title: I love it after just one day
text:
First of all, to the developer:  I read your Notion page and it seems like you really made this app through personal passion and research, so kudos! 

Secondly, this is the first routine-developing app that’s actually worked for me. I don’t know if it’s the simplicity, or the timer? But it breaks me out of my indecision paralysis before waking up/going to bed/starting studying. I don’t have ADHD I just really struggle to start anything! 

The only things that I’d note is that it’d be cool to have a feature where you have one, overarching, ‘morning routine’ and then various variations of that morning routine - a shorter one if you wake up late, one if you feel like going on a run, etc. I have the pro version so I know this is possible but it’d be good if when we did one of the various Morning routines, it would tick off the overarching Morning Routine so we know that we DID do a routine that morning even if it was shorter or slightly different. 

Also, I’m not sure about the subscription model for this app. I’m very surprised that it’s not just a one-time payment. 

Other than that, 5*!! Keep up the good work Mr./Ms. Developer!!

title: Feels like a free trial
text: This apps interface is amazing and the flow of it really works. It has helped me to remember to do everything I need to. Though it really doesn’t feel like your getting the full experience without premium. I understand the need for a premium option, but the subscription just would not work for me. Others (especially Neurodivergent people) have complained about this as well because managing subscriptions can be really hard. I’ve come up with two solutions to fix this problem that hopefully isn’t too much trouble for the developers and I sincerely hope that they take some of my recommendations to heart. My first though would be to allow for 3 routines instead of two, and/or add a setting so you can toggle certain tasks depending on the day. They could also allow for something to show up in the feedback and individual analysis pages instead of them teasing what you would have for premium. Possibly a log of the information given to you after you finish a routine. The other option which would be appreciated though wouldn’t necessarily fix the initial problem would be to implement a one time purchase option in order to make premium more accessible. Again I love the app and thank you to the developers for the amazing things that you’ve done with it.

title: 1+1 scam??
text: I saw the “1+1 promotion” for the new year and it was written there that I’ll get 6-months subscription + 6-months gift code. I thought I would be able to use the 12 months of subscription in total (using the gift code for additional 6 months) so I purchased it, but after I purchased it I found out that the gift code expires in only 3 months and I myself can’t use it (because my subscription ends in 6 months). Anybody would think they can use the gift code themselves if it’s written as “1+1”, and besides, the promotion didn’t mention anywhere that the gift code is going to expire in 3 months. This is very misleading and deceptive. I’ve been using the app for a long while now and didn’t expect that they will deceive the user with this kind of scheme. Very disappointed.
